# QS-CFW-9335-36 - Quality specification - gear blank CFW-9335-36 (8620)  
Revision: Rev F (supersedes Rev E)  
Plant: P3  
Parts: CFW-9335-36

Scope
- This document defines the quality requirements, inspection method, and nonconformance handling for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) manufactured from 8620 in Plant P3.

Requirements table

| Requirement | Specification |
|---|---|
| Material identification | 8620, traceable to batch certificate |
| Hardness range | The hardness range for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) is 36-41 HRC. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | The bore diameter tolerance for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) is ±0.04 mm. |
| Maximum forging weight | The maximum forging weight for gear blank CFW-9335-36 (CFW-9335-36) is 107.9 kg. |
| Surface condition | Free of detrimental laps, seams, and cold shuts; acceptable scale removal per standard shop practice |

Inspection method
- Visual inspection: Inspect each part for surface discontinuities and forging defects against the surface condition requirement.
- Dimensional inspection: Verify bore diameter using calibrated bore gauge or equivalent measuring device. Record measured value and confirm compliance with the bore diameter tolerance specified above.
- Hardness inspection: Verify hardness using a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester in accordance with standard practice. Ensure readings fall within the hardness range specified above. Take representative hardness measurements at locations representative of the component cross section; record individual readings with part identification.
- Weight verification: Confirm forged weight does not exceed the maximum forging weight specified above by using the plant scale and traceable measurement procedures.
- Record retention: Maintain inspection records with part identification and inspector signature in the quality system.

Nonconformance handling
- Parts that fail any requirement in the table are to be segregated, tagged, and recorded as nonconforming.
- Engineering disposition is required for all nonconforming parts; allowable dispositions include rework, repair, or scrap as authorized by engineering.
- Reworked parts must be reinspected to the same requirements and have records updated to reflect disposition and final inspection results.
- Rejects shall be disposed of or returned to processing only after documented approval.
